en: 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi al-Safar, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, from al-Bara', that whenever the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took his place of rest, he would say: "O Allah, in Your name I live and in Your name I die." And when he awakened, he would say: "All praise is for Allah Who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and unto Him is the resurrection."

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, that he heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded a man... similar to it, and he did not mention: "and if you enter morning, you will have attained good."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to a man: "O so-and-so, when you retire to your bed..." similar to the hadith of 'Amr ibn Murrah, except that he said: "and in Your Prophet whom You have sent. If you die during your night, you die upon the natural disposition (fitrah); and if you enter morning, you will have attained good."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman and Abu Dawud both narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah narrating from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded a man, when he took his place of rest at night, to say: "O Allah, I have surrendered my soul to You, turned my face to You, entrusted my back to You, and committed my affair to You, out of longing and dread toward You. There is no shelter and no refuge from You except to You. I have believed in Your Book which You revealed, and in Your Messenger whom You sent. For if he dies, he dies upon the natural disposition." And Ibn Bashshar did not mention in his hadith: "at night."

And Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: 'Abdullah—meaning Ibn Idris—narrated to us, saying: I heard Husayn, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this hadith; except that Mansur's hadith is more complete, and he added in the hadith of Husayn: "and if he enters morning, he will have attained good."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim—and the wording is 'Uthman's—narrated to us; Ishaq said: He informed us, and 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah: Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When you take your place of rest, perform your ablution as for prayer, then lie down on your right side, and then say: 'O Allah, I have surrendered my face to You, committed my affair to You, and entrusted my back to You, out of longing and dread toward You. There is no shelter and no refuge from You except to You. I have believed in Your Book which You revealed, and in Your Prophet whom You sent.' And make them your last words. Then if you die during your night, you die upon the natural disposition." He said: So I repeated them to commit them to memory and said: "I have believed in Your Messenger whom You sent." He said: "Say: 'I have believed in Your Prophet whom You sent.'"

And 'Isa ibn Hammad al-Misri narrated to me: Al-Layth informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Ja'far, from Ya'qub, that he mentioned to him that Abu Salih, mawla of Ghatafan, informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah saying: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, a scorpion stung me..." similar to the hadith of Ibn Wahb.

And Harun ibn Ma'ruf and Abu al-Tahir both narrated to us from Ibn Wahb—and the wording is Harun's: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: And 'Amr—and he is Ibn al-Harith—informed us that Yazid ibn Abi Habib and al-Harith ibn Ya'qub both narrated to him from Ya'qub ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Ashajj, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from Khawlah bint Hakim al-Sulamiyyah, that she heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "When one of you stops at a lodging place, let him say: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.' For nothing will harm him until he departs from it." Ya'qub said: And al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim said, from Dhakwan Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what distress I met from a scorpion that stung me last night!" He said: "If only you had said when you entered the evening: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,' it would not have harmed you."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us—and the wording is his: Al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from al-Harith ibn Ya'qub, that Ya'qub ibn 'Abdullah narrated to him that he heard Busr ibn Sa'id saying: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas saying: I heard Khawlah bint Hakim al-Sulamiyyah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Whoever stops at a lodging place and then says: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,' nothing will harm him until he departs from that lodging place of his."

'Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to me, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us: Sumayy narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to seek refuge from the evil decree, from the overtake of misery, from the malice of enemies, and from severe hardship. 'Amr said in his hadith: Sufyan said: I suspect that I added one of them.

Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' al-'Abdi narrated to us: Bahz ibn Asad al-'Ammi narrated to us: Harun al-A'war narrated to us: Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to make these supplications: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness, laziness, the most abject old age, the torment of the grave, and the trials of life and death."

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Ibn Mubarak informed us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he sought refuge from things that he mentioned, and miserliness.

And Abu Kamil narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Mu'tamir narrated to us; both from al-Taymi, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to it, except that Yazid's hadith does not contain his words: "and from the trials of life and death."

Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us; he said: And Sulayman al-Taymi informed us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity, laziness, cowardice, decrepitude, and miserliness; and I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave and from the trials of life and death."

And Abu al-Tahir narrated it to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: A man whom he named and 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, that he heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As saying: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a supplication with which I may supplicate in my prayer and in my house." Then he mentioned similar to the hadith of al-Layth, except that he said: "much wrong" (zulman kathiran).

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: Al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from Abu Bakr, that he said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Teach me a supplication with which I may supplicate in my prayer." He said: "Say: 'O Allah, I have wronged myself with great wrong—and Qutaybah said: much wrong—and none forgives sins except You; so forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy upon me; indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.'"

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us: 'Uthman—and he is Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us: Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "Shall I not direct you to a word from the treasures of Paradise—or he said—to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise?" I said: "Yes indeed." He said: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" (There is no power and no strength except by Allah).

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Al-Thaqafi informed us: Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Abu Musa, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on an expedition... and he mentioned the hadith, and said in it: "and the One Whom you supplicate is closer to one of you than the neck of his riding animal." And there is no mention in his hadith of: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah."

Khalaf ibn Hisham and Abu al-Rabi' both narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu 'Uthman, from Abu Musa, who said: We were with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on a journey... and he mentioned similar to the hadith of 'Asim.

And Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated it to us: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father: Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, from Abu Musa, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned similar to it.

Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn narrated to us: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us: Al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Abu Musa, that they were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while climbing up a mountain pass; he said: Whenever a man ascended a mountain pass, he called out: "La ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar" (There is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest). He said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent." He said: Then he said: "O Abu Musa—or O 'Abdullah ibn Qays—shall I not direct you to a word from the treasure of Paradise?" I said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" (There is no power and no strength except by Allah).
Ibn Numayr, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj all narrated to us from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from 'Asim with this chain of transmission, similar to it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Fudayl and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu 'Uthman, from Abu Musa, who said: We were with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on a journey, and the people began raising their voices with the takbir (Allahu Akbar). The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; indeed, you are calling upon One Who is All-Hearing, Ever-Near, and He is with you." He said: And I was behind him, saying: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" (There is no power and no strength except by Allah). He said: "O 'Abdullah ibn Qays, shall I not direct you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise?" I said: "Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Say: 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Khalid—meaning Sulayman ibn Hayyan—narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to me: Hafs—meaning Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us; all of them from Hisham; (H) and Abu Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Harb—and the wording is his—narrated to me: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever repents before the sun rises from its setting place, Allah will accept his repentance."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated it to us: My father narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Dawud and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi both narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah in this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Burdah, who said: I heard al-Agharr—and he was among the Companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—narrating to Ibn 'Umar, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O people, repent to Allah, for indeed I repent to Him one hundred times a day."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki all narrated to us from Hammad; Yahya said: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, from Thabit, from Abu Burdah, from al-Agharr al-Muzani—and he had companionship [with the Prophet]—that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, a veil comes over my heart, and indeed I ask Allah for forgiveness one hundred times a day."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Marhum ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Abu Na'amah al-Sa'di, from Abu 'Uthman, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Mu'awiyah came out to a circle in the mosque and said: "What made you sit?" They said: "We sat to remember Allah." He said: "By Allah, nothing made you sit except that?" They said: "By Allah, nothing made us sit except that." He said: "As for me, I did not make you swear out of any suspicion against you, and no one of my station from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) narrated fewer hadiths from him than me; and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) once came out to a circle of his Companions and said: 'What made you sit?' They said: 'We sat to remember Allah and to praise Him for guiding us to Islam and bestowing favor upon us through it.' He said: 'By Allah, nothing made you sit except that?' They said: 'By Allah, nothing made us sit except that.' He said: 'As for me, I did not make you swear out of any suspicion against you; rather, Gabriel came to me and informed me that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, boasts of you to the angels.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Aba Ishaq narrating from al-Agharr Abu Muslim, that he said: I bear witness concerning Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that they both bore witness concerning the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "No group of people sit remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that the angels surround them, mercy envelops them, tranquility descends upon them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him." And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us in this chain of transmission, similar to it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us; (H) and Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated it to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; they both said: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih; and in the hadith of Abu Usamah: Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... similar to the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, except that the hadith of Abu Usamah does not contain the mention of easing the hardship of someone in financial difficulty.
